notes: §1985:VII.2.11.3 GR1: "The MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause is required when more than one file shares the same physical reel of tape", only the files the program uses need be listed, the POSITION phrase is needed only when a file of the sequence is not listed, and "Not more than one file on the same tape reel may be open at one time." The clause is a hardware dependent element (§1985:p.XVII-94 item 7: "The MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause is dependent upon a reel type of device"), and §1985:I.1.5.2.5.1 lets its function go unimplemented where no such device is claimed, provided the absence is specified; docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.4 specifies it (no reel device, the placement of files on a reel a null facility, kb/Work PB5086). What the compiler does at --std 85: multipleFileClause and multipleFileTapeEntry accept the clause with any subset of the program's files, each with or without POSITION; ScreenMultipleFileClause resolves every file-name (ResolveIoControlFile, COBOL1639), refuses an empty list (COBOL5944) and records the clause as the program's statement that its files share a reel (FileModel.MultipleFileReels), which the statement rules that are decidable from the source read: OPEN EXTEND of such a file (CheckOpenModeForFile, COBOL6814), a non-sequential file in the set, and MERGE over two files of one clause (ScreenMultipleFileReels). VisitMultipleFileClause is the edition arm (accepted at 85, COBOL0902 from 2002). The last sentence is a constraint on the running program for which the text defines no result; with no reel it constrains nothing, and section 3.4 records one-file-open-at-a-time as part of the null facility. Probed at 85: FILE-B POSITION 1 FILE-C POSITION 3 beside a file not listed compiles, and the two listed files open at the same time, are written and read back; OPEN EXTEND of a listed file is refused (COBOL6814). The witness lists two files without POSITION and writes and reads one of them.

next.reason: 1985: "The MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause is required when more than one file shares the same physical reel of tape."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause; no candidate covers files sharing a reel or the POSITION phrase.". No 2023 clause holds this feature. The SAME clause's one-file-open rule is about shared memory areas, not files sharing a tape reel, so the clause is dropped.
